title: Projection Area of 3D Shapes
description:
You are given an `n x n` integer matrix `grid` where we place stacks of `1 x 1 x 1` cubes aligned with the `x`, `y`, and `z` axes. Specifically, `grid[i][j]` represents a vertical tower of `grid[i][j]` cubes placed on top of grid cell `(i, j)`.

We view the **projection** (shadow) of these cubes onto the `xy`, `yz`, and `zx` planes:
- The `xy` (top) projection area equals the number of cells `(i, j)` with `grid[i][j] > 0`.
- The `yz` (front) projection area equals the sum of the maximum value in each row.
- The `zx` (side) projection area equals the sum of the maximum value in each column.

Return the total area of all three projections combined.
hints: In a single double loop over i and j, count non-zero cells while tracking rowMax = max_j grid[i][j] and colMax = max_j grid[j][i].
Add rowMax and colMax to the total area at the end of each outer iteration i, using O(1) extra space.

examples.explanation: Top area = 4 (all 4 cells > 0), front area = 2 + 4 = 6, side area = 3 + 4 = 7; total = 4 + 6 + 7 = 17.
A single tower of height 2 has top area 1, front area 2, and side area 2, totaling 5.
Top area = 2 (two non-zero cells), front area = 1 + 2 = 3, side area = 1 + 2 = 3; total = 8.
